title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is §45 (archive page 384) of the 'équation des lacets' notes (c. 1981–82). Here Γ̃ is Grothendieck's group of solutions of the loop equations, his precursor of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^. 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} is a profinite 'Teichmüller-type' group: an extension of 𝔖_3 by the profinite fundamental group Π^_{0,3} of P^1−{0,1,∞}, which is free profinite on two generators. The next page identifies it with SL(2,Z)^, the orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1} over Q̄.

Definitions on this page:
- M̃_{0,3} is the group of automorphisms 'à lacets' of 𝔖̂^+_{0,3}, meaning those preserving the classes of the standard loops, that induce the trivial outer action on 𝔖_3 = 𝔖̂^+_{0,3}/Π^_{0,3}.
- Ñ_{0,3} is the corresponding group of outer automorphisms inducing the identity on 𝔖_3.
- This gives an extension (1): 1 → 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} (inner automorphisms) → M̃_{0,3} → Ñ_{0,3} → 1. Implicitly Ñ_{0,3} ≅ Γ̃, which is why the title calls M̃ the extension Ñ_{1,1} of Γ̃ by SL(2,Z)^.

An arithmetic remark follows. Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) embeds in Γ̃ (Belyi), and its inverse image in (1) is the arithmetic group M_{0,3}, i.e. essentially π_1 of the stack M_{1,1} over Q, an extension of G_Q by SL(2,Z)^. Grothendieck then remarks, as best the handwriting can be read, that there is for the moment no plausible characterization of Γ_Q as a subgroup of Γ̃. This is the open problem GT^ ≟ G_Q.

He then announces a canonical splitting of (1). It is given by the subgroup Γ̃_σ (written Π̃_σ in the next-page transcription) of automorphisms commuting with a fixed element (σ_0 or τ_∞). This is the group-theoretic analogue of a (tangential) rational base point, and it makes M̃_{0,3} a semidirect product SL(2,Z)^ ⋊ Γ̃_σ.

The purpose, completed on the next page, is to extend the Tate-module representation π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) → GL(2,Ẑ) to a homomorphism M̃_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' defined on the whole GT-type extension. It is the product of:
- the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ), and
- an explicit formula u ↦ μ[[u, εt],[−t, εu]] on Γ̃_σ, built from the 'lacet' invariants t, u, μ, ε of the previous section.
errors: Numbering: the page number is 384 (previous page 383), not 389.
The kernel in (1) should be the inner automorphism group, i.e. 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} itself (as the next page's semidirect product confirms), not Π_{0,3}. The handwriting seems overwritten there.

Identifying the inner automorphism group with 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ ignores its centre ±1. Strictly the kernel is SL(2,Z)^/centre unless a convention handles −1. This is a possible gap, not addressed on the page.
That Ñ_{0,3} ≅ Γ̃ is used implicitly and not proved on the page.

ideas.what: Group-theoretic extension of Γ̃ (≈GT^) by SL(2,Z)^, built as automorphisms à lacets of the profinite orbifold group, generalizing π_1(M_{1,1}/Q) with G_Q replaced by Γ̃
ideas.modern_name: GT^-analogue of the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1}; GT acting on SL(2,Z)^ / B_3^ (genus-one level of the Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; for genus one: Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and the GT idea in general terms

ideas.what: Inverse image of Γ_Q in the Γ̃-extension recovers the arithmetic group M_{0,3}; remark that no plausible characterization of Γ_Q inside Γ̃ is available
ideas.where_published: Esquisse hints at describing G_Q via the tower

ideas.what: Canonical splitting of the extension via the centralizer of a fixed element (σ_0/τ_∞), the analogue of a tangential base point
ideas.modern_name: Section of π_1 given by a (tangential) rational base point

ideas.what: Homomorphism M̃_{0,3} → GL(2,Ẑ)' extending the Tate-module (congruence) representation to the GT-type extension, with explicit matrix μ[[u, εt],[−t, εu]] (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Extension of the elliptic Galois representation / congruence quotient to GT^-actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Nakamura's and Lochak–Schneps' genus-one GT work (unsure of exact source)

missed.claim: Around 1981–82 Grothendieck explicitly constructed the extension of his group Γ̃ (≈GT^) by SL(2,Z)^, i.e. a GT-version of π_1(M_{1,1,Q}). He did so with a canonical splitting and a map to GL(2,Ẑ), roughly a decade before Drinfeld's GT and before the genus-one GT literature (Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps).
missed.quote: construction de l'extension Ñ_{1,1} de Γ̃ par Sl(2,Z)^
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for genus-one GT actions. The explicit matrix formula on the next page may offer a concrete description of the 'GT Tate-module representation', comparable with the elliptic GT of Enriquez and with Hain–Matsumoto's work.

missed.claim: Grothendieck notes the lack of any plausible intrinsic characterization of Γ_Q inside Γ̃. This is the still-open question of whether GT^ equals G_Q.
missed.quote: pour le moment ... pas de caractérisation bien plausible propre de Γ_Q comme sous-groupe de Γ̃
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck explicitly posed the GT^ vs G_Q problem in his private notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mostly definitional. It does, however, document an early, explicit construction of the genus-one GT-type extension of Γ̃ by SL(2,Z)^ and its GL(2,Ẑ)-representation, which the literature credits to work from the 1990s and later. The ideas are known today, but this unpublished priority detail is notable.
transcription_corrections: 'mais pour le moment ça n'est pas des continuités bien plausibles ! proposer de Γ_Q' should read approximately 'mais pour le moment on n'a pas de caractérisation bien plausible propre de Γ_Q comme sous-groupe de Γ̃'.
In (1) the kernel term appears to be 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} (a 'Π' overwritten), consistent with the next page's semidirect product.
'sous-groupe Γ̃_0 de M' is probably 'Γ̃_σ de M̃'; the final symbol 'σ_0' may be 'τ_∞' (uncertain).
The margin note seems to redefine M_{0,3} as automorphisms (not outer) à lacets that fix the classes of loops and induce the identity on 𝔖_3, with N_{0,3} the corresponding outer version.
